questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify the SI base unit of time
questions.stem: Which of the following is the SI base unit of time?

options.text: The minute, because it is the unit used in most timetables
options.misconception: confuses a common multiple with the base unit

options.text: The second, fixed by a set count of caesium-133 radiation periods
The hour, because it divides the day into twenty-four parts
options.misconception: treats a derived subdivision as the base unit

options.text: The day, because it is the largest unit of time in general use
options.misconception: confuses the reference interval with the base unit

questions.explanation: The second is the SI base unit of time, fixed by counting periods of radiation from the caesium-133 hyperfine transition. Minutes and hours are derived from it, so they are not base units.
questions.hint: Look for the unit the others are built from.

options.text: The conversion factor was skipped; 72 km per hour is 20 m per second
The unit prefix was dropped; 72 km per hour is 72000 m per second
options.misconception: treats the prefix as the only thing to change

options.text: The divisor was wrong; 72 km per hour is 2.8 m per second
options.misconception: divides by 1000 but forgets the hour in seconds

options.text: Nothing is wrong; the numeric value carries over between speed units
options.misconception: assumes the number is unchanged by the unit

45 km per hour, because the two hourly figures are averaged
options.misconception: averages the hourly speeds without checking the equal times

questions.explanation: Average speed is total distance over total time, so 100 km in 2 hours gives 50 km per hour. Averaging the two hourly speeds works here only because each hour is the same length.

questions.explanation: Acceleration has dimensions of length per time squared, L T to the minus two. Speed is length per time, and adding or removing a factor of time is what separates the two.

options.misconception: claims acceleration has no time dependence

options.misconception: believes dimensional checks cannot be applied to formulas

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: List the SI base units for length, mass and time
questions.stem: A student lists the SI base units for length, mass and time. Which row is correct?

options.text: Metre, kilogram and minute, because minutes divide the day evenly
options.misconception: treats a convenient subdivision as a base unit

options.text: Metre, kilogram and second, because the others are built from them
Kilometre, kilogram and hour, because those are used in daily life
options.misconception: chooses the units of everyday practice

options.text: Metre, gram and second, because grams measure mass more finely
options.misconception: confuses a prefixed unit with a base unit

questions.explanation: The SI base units for length, mass and time are the metre, the kilogram and the second. Kilometres, grams and minutes are derived from them by prefixes or defined multiples, so none is a base unit.
questions.hint: Base units are the ones others are built from.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a prefixed capacitance into another prefixed unit

questions.explanation: A micro is a millionth and a pico is a trillionth, so a microfarad is a million picofarads and 4.7 of them is 4700000 pF. Swapping the two prefixes changes the value by a factor of a million.
questions.hint: A microfarad is a million picofarads.

The method is right and gives 5.4 km per hour, because the factor is 3.6

options.text: The method is wrong and gives 150 km per hour, because the factor is 10
options.misconception: invents a conversion factor of ten

options.text: The method is wrong and gives 54 km per hour, because hours are longer than seconds
options.misconception: rejects the correct factor for the wrong reason

questions.explanation: Multiplying metres per second by 3.6 converts to kilometres per hour, so 15 m per second is 54 km per hour. The same value expressed the other way round would be divided by 3.6.
questions.hint: Metres per second times 3.6 gives kilometres per hour.

questions.stem: A courier log shows four legs: 30 km in 30 min, 30 km in 45 min, 20 km in 20 min and 20 km in 40 min. What is the average speed for the whole trip?

options.text: 45 km per hour, because the four leg speeds average to that value
options.misconception: averages the leg speeds without regard to their times

options.text: 50 km per hour, because the total distance is 100 km in 2 hours
options.misconception: rounds the total time to a convenient value

options.text: 44.4 km per hour, because 100 km took 135 minutes in total
40 km per hour, because the slowest leg sets the pace for the trip
options.misconception: uses the slowest leg speed as the average

questions.explanation: The legs total 100 km and 135 minutes, which is 2.25 hours, so the average speed is 44.4 km per hour. Averaging the leg speeds overstates it because the slower legs took longer.
questions.hint: Add the distances and add the times separately.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: State what a dimensional analysis check establishes
questions.stem: What does a dimensional analysis check tell you about a proposed formula?

options.text: It checks that both sides can be expressed in the same units, not that the physics is right
It proves the formula is correct whenever the units match on both sides
options.misconception: believes a matching check proves the physics

options.text: It shows that the formula cannot be used because units are never balanced
options.misconception: presumes dimensional checks always fail

options.text: It replaces the need to measure the quantities the formula describes
options.misconception: claims analysis removes the need for experiment

questions.explanation: A dimensional check confirms only that the units can balance, so a wrong formula with the right dimensions still passes. The physics must be established separately, by reasoning or by measurement.
questions.hint: Matching units is necessary but not sufficient.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a speed in dimensionally correct units
questions.stem: A cheetah covers 100 m in 5.0 s. Its speed in metres per second is what value?
questions.explanation: Speed is distance divided by time, so 100 / 5.0 = 20 m per second, and metres per second matches the dimensions of length over time. Kilometres per hour would describe the same speed as 72.
questions.hint: Divide the distance by the time.

options.text: The objection is wrong, because squaring the radius gives the length squared that area needs
The objection is right, because area should involve length not length squared
options.misconception: believes area has dimensions of length only

options.text: The objection is right, because pi has no units so the formula cannot balance
options.misconception: thinks a dimensionless factor spoils the balance

options.text: The objection is wrong, but only because pi is an irrational number
options.misconception: confuses the reason with a property of the constant

questions.explanation: Area has dimensions of length squared and squaring the radius produces exactly those, so the formula passes the check. A dimensionless factor such as pi changes only the number, never the dimensions.
questions.hint: Squaring a length gives the dimensions of area.

questions.learningObjective: Compare force per unit mass for two bodies
questions.stem: Two trolleys are compared: one of mass 8 kg pushed with 40 N, another of mass 16 kg pushed with 40 N. What do the force per unit mass figures show?

options.text: Both trolleys accelerate equally, because the same force acts on each
options.misconception: ignores the different masses in the comparison

options.text: The heavier trolley accelerates faster, because it carries more load
options.misconception: claims more mass means more acceleration at equal force

options.text: The lighter trolley accelerates twice as fast, at 5 against 2.5 N per kg
The figures show nothing, because force per unit mass has no unit
options.misconception: denies that the ratio carries a unit

questions.explanation: Force per unit mass is 40 / 8 = 5 N per kilogram for the lighter trolley and 40 / 16 = 2.5 for the heavier, so the lighter accelerates twice as fast. Equal forces do not give equal accelerations when the masses differ.
questions.hint: Divide each force by the mass that carries it.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify the error caused by using the wrong base unit
questions.stem: A control log records intervals in hours, minutes and seconds. A converter wrongly treats the hour as the SI base unit. What error results?

options.text: No error arises, because the hour is the largest unit used in the log
options.misconception: equates frequent use with base status

options.text: Every interval is off by a factor of 3600, because the second is the base unit
Only the seconds column is affected, because hours are already divided
options.misconception: assumes only small units cause trouble

options.text: The log becomes unusable, because mixed units cannot be converted
options.misconception: claims conversion between units is impossible

questions.explanation: The second is the base unit and the hour is 3600 of them, so treating the hour as a base unit scales every converted value by 3600. Mixed units can always be converted once the base unit is known.
questions.hint: The base unit is the one everything else counts.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the prefix meaning one thousandth
questions.stem: Which prefix on a unit means one thousandth of that unit?

options.text: Kilo, because it multiplies the unit by a thousand
options.misconception: confuses the direction of the kilo prefix

options.text: Mega, because it multiplies the unit by a million
options.misconception: confuses the mega prefix with milli

options.text: Centi, because it divides the unit by a hundred
options.misconception: confuses centi with milli

options.text: Milli, because it divides the unit by a thousand

questions.explanation: Milli means one thousandth, so a millimetre is a thousandth of a metre, while kilo means a thousand times and mega a million times. Centi is a hundredth, so it is easy to mix up with milli.
questions.hint: Milli means a thousandth of the unit.

questions.topic: Average speed from a trip log
questions.learningObjective: Identify when averaging leg speeds gives the wrong answer
questions.stem: A learner computes an average speed by adding the speeds of each leg and dividing by the number of legs. When does that give the wrong answer?

options.text: It is always wrong, even when all the legs take the same time
options.misconception: rules out the case where the mean is correct

options.text: It is wrong whenever any leg has a different length
options.misconception: ties the error to distances rather than times

options.text: It is wrong whenever the speeds are all different from each other
options.misconception: confuses differing speeds with unequal times

options.text: It is wrong whenever the legs take different amounts of time

questions.explanation: The mean of the leg speeds equals the true average only when every leg occupies the same time, since the mean then also matches total distance over total time. With unequal times the slower legs are underweighted.

questions.learningObjective: Check the dimensions of a time formula
questions.stem: A proposed formula for the time of a journey is written as t equals distance divided by speed. Which dimensional statement does this satisfy?

options.text: It is dimensionally wrong, because time cannot be written with distance in it
options.misconception: believes distance cannot appear in a time formula

options.text: It is dimensionally sound, since length over length per time gives time
It is dimensionally wrong, because speed already contains a time factor
options.misconception: misreads how the time factors cancel

options.text: It is dimensionally sound, but only because the units of speed are undefined
options.misconception: relies on units being undefined

questions.explanation: Distance has dimensions of length and speed has dimensions of length per time, so their quotient has dimensions of time. The check passes, though the physics still has to be justified.
questions.hint: Divide the dimensions of distance by those of speed.

questions.stem: A circular pond has a radius of 7 m. Using pi as 3.142, its area in square metres is what value?

It should be in newtons per second, since force changes with time
options.misconception: invents a time dimension for force

options.misconception: inverts the ratio to match a mass figure

questions.learningObjective: Explain why a base unit must be defined independently
questions.stem: A definition writes the second as one sixtieth of a minute. Why is that statement incomplete as a definition of an SI base unit?

options.text: It only relates the second to another unit, rather than fixing it independently

options.misconception: misreads the relationship between minute and second

options.text: It is incomplete because the second must be defined using a pendulum
